# NexaLayer agent integration summary

Base URL: `https://api.nexalayer.net/v1`

Authentication uses `X-API-Key`; no refresh token is required. A new email can request a Key at `POST /account/request-api-key` and receives one small automatic trial credit. Repeated requests resend the same Key and do not grant another trial.

Before signup, call unauthenticated `GET /public/products` and read each product's current numeric USD `price` and `unit`. Before spending, call authenticated `GET /products`. Configure `PUT /account/budget` with key and daily limits. Use `GET /account/usage-alerts` for threshold events. All writes should carry an `Idempotency-Key`.

The core lifecycle is: list products, create a Session, poll its status, request proxy credentials with `include_credentials=true` only in the process that will connect, report telemetry, read health and usage, rotate only when appropriate, and terminate resources when finished. `GET /sessions/{session_id}` and rotate omit `proxy.username`, `proxy.password`, and `proxy.full_url` unless that query flag is true. Create does not accept the flag.

Launch pricing, subject to change and not a quote: dynamic `$0.23/GB`, shared static from `$1.05/month`, exclusive static `$1.43–$5.86/month`. The live products API is authoritative. HTTP 409 `PRICE_MISMATCH` means the price changed since the read, no order was placed, and the agent must re-read prices before retrying. Other codes, HTTP statuses, and retry actions: https://docs.nexalayer.net/en/errors.

MCP clients can run `npx -y @nexalayer/mcp` with `NEXALAYER_API_KEY` in the process environment. Paid creation and budget changes should remain owner-approved.

The current production model is human-funded, agent-controlled spending: an owner funds the account and the agent spends only within owner-defined budgets. USDT TRC20 recharge is exposed through API order creation and status polling, but an agent still needs an authorized wallet. x402 is under evaluation and is not currently advertised as live.

NexaLayer processes operational metadata and optional telemetry, not page payload bodies by design. Do not put cookies, credentials, page content, personal data, or proxy URLs in telemetry or logs.
